tool.name: RSEM calculate expression
tool.command: mkdir reference && rsem-prepare-reference #if str($reference.source) == 'genome': --gtf '$reference.gtf' #elif $reference.transcript_to_gene_map: --transcript-to-gene-map '$reference.transcript_to_gene_map' #end if '$reference.fasta' reference/rsem > rsem.log && rsem-sam-validator '$alignments' > validation.log && cat validation.log >> rsem.log && ## RSEM 1.3.3's validator also returns zero for invalid input. if ! grep -qFx 'The input file is valid!' validation.log; then cat validation.log >&2; exit 1; fi && rsem-calculate-expression --alignments --num-threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} #if str($library.layout) == 'paired': --paired-end #else: --fragment-length-mean $library.fragment_length_mean --fragment-length-sd $library.fragment_length_sd #end if --strandedness '$strandedness' --seed-length $advanced.seed_length $advanced.estimate_rspd $advanced.append_names #if str($output_bam) == 'false': --no-bam-output #end if '$alignments' reference/rsem rsem_out >> rsem.log

param.label: Transcriptome alignments
param.help: Use transcript coordinates, for example STAR's Aligned.toTranscriptome.out.bam. Alignments for each read must be grouped together, with paired mates adjacent. Genomic alignments are unsuitable.

param.name: fasta
param.label: Reference genome
param.help: Use the same genome assembly that was used for alignment.

param.label: Gene annotation
param.help: Use the same annotation and transcript identifiers that were used to produce the transcriptome alignments.

param.name: fasta
param.label: Reference transcripts
param.help: Sequence identifiers, lengths, and sequences must match the alignment reference.

param.label: Transcript-to-gene map
param.help: Two whitespace-separated columns without a header: gene ID, then transcript ID. Without a map, each transcript is treated as a separate gene.

param.label: Mean fragment length
param.help: For single-end data, provide the mean fragment length in bases when known. The default of -1 disables the fragment-length distribution.

param.label: Fragment-length standard deviation
param.help: Provide the standard deviation in bases. A value of 0 assumes a fixed fragment length when a mean is specified.

param.label: Library strandedness
param.help: For paired-end libraries, orientation refers to the first mate relative to the transcript. Illumina TruSeq Stranded libraries normally use reverse.

param.label: Minimum read length
param.help: Reads shorter than this value are ignored. For paired-end reads, both mates must meet the threshold.

param.label: Estimate the read start position distribution
param.help: The default assumes a uniform distribution of read start positions.

param.label: Append gene and transcript names to identifiers
param.help: Names are appended when present in the GTF annotation.

param.name: output_bam
param.label: Output posterior-weighted transcriptome BAM
param.help: Includes alignments annotated with posterior probabilities. This output remains unsorted and uses transcript coordinates.

tool.help:
RSEM estimates gene and isoform abundance from RNA-seq alignments, accounting for reads that align to multiple transcripts.
**Inputs**
Supply a SAM or BAM file aligned to transcripts. For STAR, select **Aligned.toTranscriptome.out.bam**, generated with the TranscriptomeSAM quantification option. The aligner must use RSEM-compatible settings, including no gapped alignments. The reference transcript identifiers, sequences, and lengths must match those in the alignment file.
Alignments for the same read must occur together. For paired-end data, the two mates of each alignment must be adjacent. This tool runs `rsem-sam-validator` before estimation. If the input fails validation because of its order, prepare it with RSEM's `convert-sam-for-rsem` utility. Coordinate-sorted genomic BAM files are unsuitable.
Choose either the genome FASTA and GTF used to produce the alignments, or the corresponding transcript FASTA. A transcript-to-gene map has two columns without a header, with the gene identifier first and transcript identifier second. Without a GTF or gene map, each transcript is treated as a separate gene. The tool builds its RSEM reference in the job directory.
Select the library layout and strandedness explicitly. Single-end estimation benefits from known fragment-length mean and standard deviation. Paired-end estimation learns the fragment-length distribution from the aligned mates.
-----
**Outputs**
The gene and isoform tables contain identifiers, lengths, effective lengths, expected counts, TPM, and FPKM. Isoform estimates also include the percentage of the parent gene's expression assigned to that isoform. Expected counts can be fractional because RSEM assigns ambiguous reads probabilistically.
The log records reference preparation, alignment validation, and estimation. An optional unsorted transcriptome BAM contains posterior alignment probabilities in the `ZW` tag.
See the [RSEM documentation](https://deweylab.github.io/RSEM/) for reference preparation and alignment requirements.
